1 1.

This case was registered on the basis of statement of complainant Sh. Krishan Mahato recorded by Executive Magistrate in which he stated that his daughter Sandhya (deceased) married with accused Bhirgu Nath Mahto on 06.05.2019.
Father of his son-in-law was not well and on 23 rd January he went to meet him at Mata Chanan Devi Hospital where his daughter was also present.
When he asked about wellness of his daughter, she remained silent.
Thereafter, father- in-law of his daughter was referred to another hospital.
He again went to meet him in that hospital on 26th January at about 2.30 pm where mother-in-law and brother-in-law of his daughter were present alongwith 2-3 persons.
At about 3.10 pm, mother-in-law of his daughter received a call on her phone that his daughter (deceased) jumped from roof and she was being taken to Mata Chanan Devi Hospital.
He went to that hospital where he was not told anything by anybody.
When doctor had given ornaments of his daughter to him, then he came to know that his daughter had expired.
His son-in-law had also not told him anything.
On 25th January he received a call from his son-in-law i.e. accused Bhirgu and he asked him to take his daughter with him.
When he (complainant) asked about the reason, he had not told anything and he had also not allowed him to talk with his daughter because his daughter was at home and his son-in-law was at hospital.
He further stated in his statement that he is having doubt that his daughter-in-law had killed his daughter.
He also stated that mother-in-law of his daughter always used to taunt her that her parents had not taught her anything.

2. On the basis of statement of the complainant as well as the factum of the death of deceased and the medical documents, the FIR No.50/2020 under Section 304B/498A IPC was registered at PS Janak Puri.
After completion of investigation, chargesheet was filed against both accused persons i.e. Bhirgu Mahato and Gayatri Devi for the offence punishable under Section 304B/498A IPC.
3. Accused persons were summoned after taking cognizance.
After compliance of section 207 Cr.P.C., the case was committed to the Court of Sessions.

After hearing arguments on the point of charge and on the basis of prima-facie evidence, charge was framed against the accused persons Bhirgu Mahato and Gayatri Devi for the offence punishable under Sections 498A/304B IPC to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
4. In order to substantiate the charge, prosecution has filed list of 14 witnesses and examined 5 witnesses.
5. PW1 Sh. Krishan Mahato is the complainant/father of the deceased.
He deposed that his daughter Sandhya was married to accused Bhirgu Mahato on 06.05.2019.
She was happily residing in her in-laws family.
Her father-in-law was ill and was admitted in Balaji Hospital at Peera Garhi.
On 26.01.2020 he and his wife went to see him.
Mother-in-law of his daughter i.e. accused Gayatri Devi was also present there who received a call that complainant's daughter fell down from roof of the house.
Then he alongwith elder brother of accused Bhirgu reached at Mata Chanan Devi Hospital where his daughter was taken for treatment by accused Bhirgu.
He asked from Bhirgu that what happened.
At that time, Bhirgu was crying and could not tell the reason.

Thereafter, he was called inside the hospital and saw his daughter was lying on the bed inside the curtain to whom he State vs . : Bhirgu Mahato & Anr. on 18 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28906475/
2 identified as his daughter.
Then, he was sent outside.
After about half-an-hour, hospital staff demanded money from him for taabut/kafan and then he came to know that his daughter had been expired.
He was not having sufficient money and hospital staff had arranged for the kafan and body was sent to DDU Hospital where postmortem was conducted on next day and body was given to them.
Cremation was done near the hospital in the presence of them as well as in- laws family of his daughter.
6. PW1/complainant has not stated anything else.
Thereafter he was cross examined by ld. Addl. PP for the State wherein he admitted that his statement Ex.PW1/A was recorded by the Executive Magistrate on 27.01.2020.
7. PW2 Smt. Teetri Devi is mother of the deceased who had also deposed identical version as of PW1.
He was also cross examined by ld. Addl. PP for the State wherein she admitted that she made a statement Ex.PW2/A to the Executive Magistrate on 27.01.2020.
8. PW3 is Insp.

Satyender Dhull is the IO of the case who stated that on 26.01.2020, he was posted at PS Janakpuri and on that day, DD No. 30A regarding bringing of dead body of one Smt. Sandhya was received, which was marked to SI Raj Kumar who reached at Mata Chanan Devi Hospital and collected MLC of deceased.
Thereafter, SI Raj Kumar had visited at the spot i.e. A-1/7, P & T Colony.
He further stated that Insp. Shiv Kumar and Mobile Crime Team was also called at the spot and inspection of spot was also got done.
Photographs were taken and exhibits were also lifted.
As the death had occurred within eight months of marriage, the concerned SDM was also requested to come, however, due to Delhi Assembly Election at that time, he could not come.
Thereafter, the dead body was sent to DDU Hospital for postmortem.
On 27.01.2020, Executive Magistrate as per the direction of concerned SDM had come to PS.
Parents of deceased were also joined.
They had also visited the spot.
After postmortem, dead body was handed over to relatives.
Concerned Executive Magistrate had recorded statement of father of deceased and had directed the SHO to proceed as per law.
On the basis of statement of father of deceased Ex.PW1/A, he had prepared Tehrir Ex.PW3/A and got the present case registered.
The statement of mother of deceased was also recorded by Executive Magistrate which is Ex.PW2/A.
Draftsman was called at the spot and detailed site plan was got prepared.
During course of investigation, proof of marriage i.e. marriage card along with photographs were collected.
Husband of the deceased was called and he was joined into investigation.
During investigation, one Dileep was also joined.
On 27.09.2020, the father-in-law and mother-in-law of deceased had handed over the articles to the father of deceased and her aunty vide handing over memos Ex.PW3/B and Ex.PW3/C.
On 29.11.2020, cash of Rs.1,00,000/- was handed over to the father of the deceased and receipt Ex.PW3/D in this regard was prepared.
During investigation, father of deceased had handed over two pages regarding the writing of deceased which was seized vide seizure memo Ex.PW3/E.

The said writing/pages are Ex.PW3/F1 &
Ex.PW3/F2.
Accused Bhirgu had also handed over two pages which were seized vide memo Ex.PW3/G.
The said pages are Ex.PW3/G1 & Ex.PW3/G2.
He further stated that the writings along with suicide notice were sent to FSL Rohini.
The parents of the deceased had executed one affidavit which was duly notarized dated 30.12.2020 and the same was handed over to him which he placed on record.
During investigation, he had recorded statements of witnesses in present case and after completion of investigation, charge-sheet was filed in the Court.

3 9.
PW4 SI Raj Kumar is the 1st IO of the case who deposed that on 26.01.2020, he was posted at PS Janakpuri.
On that day, DD No.30A regarding brought dead of one Sandhya was received in the PS which was marked to him.
Thereafter, he alongwith staff had reached at Mata Chanan Devi Hospital and collected the MLC of deceased Sandhya.
At the hospital, he came to know regarding the spot from where the deceased had jumped and later on he had reached at the spot i.e. A-1/7, P & T Colony, Janakpuri.
Crime team was also called at the spot and he collected the crime team report and the exhibits.
He seized the blood control/sample vide seizure memo Ex.PW4/A.
One dairy Ex.P1 was also seized vide seizure memo Ex.PW4/B.
He also stated that Insp. Investigation Shiv Kumar had also joined.
One mobile phone make Redmi was seized vide seizure memo Ex.PW4/C.
Concerned SDM was also contacted but due to Delhi Assembly Election, he could not physically come on that day.
Dead body of deceased was got preserved and sent to DDU Hospital for postmortem.
Later on, the concerned Executive Magistrate had come to PS.
The parents of the deceased were also called.

Further proceedings in the present case were conducted by Insp.
Satyender Dhull.
During investigation, the postmortem of deceased was got conducted and dead body was handed over to husband of deceased.
10. PW5 HC Satish Kumar is the Photographer in the Mobile Crime Team and he had taken the photographs at the spot on 26.01.2020.

He proved the CD of the said photographs as Ex.PW5/A.
11.

Vide joint statement of both accused persons recorded separately on 07.02.2023 under Section 294 CrPC, they had admitted the genuineness of following formal documents without prejudice to their defence :-
(i) Copy of FIR No.50/2020 as Ex.PX1.
(ii) Certificate u/s 65-B of I.E. Act as Ex.PX2.
(iii) Copy of GD No. 30A dated 26.01.2020 as Ex.PX3.
(iv) Copy of GD No. 41A dated 27.01.2020 as Ex.PX4.
(v) Copy of GD No.44A dated 27.01.2020 as Ex.PX5.
(vi) Copy of Crime Visit Report as Ex.PX6.
(vii) Copy of FSL Report dated 12.08.2021 as Ex.PX7.
(viii) Copy of Scaled Site Plan dated 30.03.2020 as Ex.PX8 (Colly) (2 Pages).

(ix) MLC No.10879/20 dated 26.01.2020 of Sandhya as Ex.PX9.
(x) Copy of handing over memo of dead body as Ex.PX10.
( xi )
Copy of PM Report No.149/2020 of Sandhya as Ex.PX11.
State vs . : Bhirgu Mahato & Anr. on 18 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28906475/
4 (xii) Copy of Marriage Card and Photographs of Marriage as Ex.PX12 (Colly).

(xiii) Copy of affidavit given by Krishan Mahto and Titri Devi as Ex.PX13.
12.
The witnesses regarding the aforesaid admitted documents were dropped being unnecessary.
After examination of aforesaid five witnesses, another formal witness Sh. Hari Lal Prasad was dropped at the application moved by the IO.
Thereafter, PE was closed.

13. Statement of both accused persons recorded under Section 313 CrPC in which they denied all the allegations levelled against them and not opted for D.E.
14.
Final arguments heard.
Ld. Addl. PP for the State argued that public witnesses deliberately not supported the prosecution version.
However, they had admitted their statements recorded by the concerned SDM/Executive Magistrate in which there are clear allegations regarding the offence of cruelty and dowry death.

Prosecution has proved its case against both the accused persons and they are liable to be convicted for the offence punishable under Section 498A/304B IPC.
15.
On the other hand, ld. counsel for accused persons argued that both the accused persons have been falsely implicated by the police only to harass them.
There is no allegation either of cruelty with the deceased allegedly committed by the accused persons or regarding dowry death.
During evidence, prosecution has failed to place on record any evidence against the accused persons.
The main public witnesses including complainant had not stated anything incriminating against any of the accused.
Therefore, both accused persons are liable to be acquitted.
16. I have considered the submissions of both parties and have perused the record.

The charge against both accused persons are that they both being husband and mother-in-law respectively of deceased Sandhya subjected her to cruelty and harassment for demand of dowry and accordingly committed the offence punishable under Section 498A IPC.

Charge is also against them that the deceased Sandhya had committed suicide due to the cruelty and harassment by the accused persons soon before her death in connection with demand of dowry and as she had died in circumstances other than the natural death within seven years of her marriage and accordingly, both accused persons are also liable for the offence of dowry death punishable under Section 304B IPC.
17.

After death of the deceased, statements of father of the deceased Sh. Krishan Mahato and mother of the deceased Smt. Teetri Devi were recorded by the Executive Magistrate in which they had narrated about the circumstances and facts qua the death of deceased.
Therefore, case of prosecution is mainly based upon the statements of both these witnesses.
18. Father of the deceased Sh. Krishan Mahato was examined as PW1.
In his statement before the Court, PW1 had not raised any allegation against the accused persons and had not supported the prosecution version.

Although he had admitted that his statement Ex.PW1/A was recorded by the concerned SDM, but during his cross examination on behalf of prosecution, he clarified that this statement was given by him to the Executive Magistrate under influence of some relatives.

During State vs . : Bhirgu Mahato & Anr. on 18 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28906475/
5
his cross examination, his another statement recorded by the police on 02.09.2020 Mark-PW1/X was put to him but he denied of having been given any such statement.
He had specifically denied the suggestion that mother-in-law of the deceased used to taunt her and he raised suspicion that accused Bhirgu Mahato might have killed his daughter.

19. Another main witness of the prosecution is PW2 Smt. Teetri Devi i.e. mother of the deceased but she had also not supported the prosecution version and had not stated any incriminating fact against any of the accused.
During cross examination by ld. Addl.PP for State, she has admitted that she had given statement Ex.PW2/A to the Executive Magistrate.
As per contents of Ex.PW2/A

, she stated that her mother-in-law used to harass her daughter for dowry and she raised suspicion that her son-in-law might have killed her daughter and she had also mentioned in the statement that her daughter used to tell her through phone that accused persons used to harass her.

However, when she was confronted with this statement Ex.PW2/A, she had clearly stated that although she had given this statement to the Executive Magistrate but this statement is not correct as she made such statement under influence of some of her relatives and under trauma of death of her daughter.
She was also confronted with her statement Mark-PW2/X recorded under Section 161 CrPC but she had denied having made any such statement to the police.
20. PW3 and PW4 are the IOs who deposed about the procedural aspect of the investigation.
The documents proved on record by PW3 and PW4 are independently not sufficient to make liable the accused persons for the offence alleged against them.

The documents admitted by the accused persons under Section 294 CrPC are also formal procedural documents and they are independently not sufficient to prove the necessary ingredients of the offences charged against the accused persons.
21. It is a settled law that it is the duty of the prosecution to prove the case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
However, in view of aforesaid discussion, Court comes at the conclusion that prosecution had failed to prove its case against the accused persons due to lack of evidence.

22. Hence, both the accused persons namely Bhirgu Mahato and Gayatri Devi stand acquitted in present case FIR No.50/2020, PS Janak Puri, under Sections 498A/304B IPC.
23.

Accused persons are directed to furnish fresh bail bonds and surety bonds u/s 437-A Cr.P.C.
